content.value: Trace the initialization/test/body/update cycle; choose correct counting ranges; explain loop-variable scope.

A for loop groups initialization, continuation condition, and update in its header. Initialization runs once. The condition is tested before each body execution. After the body, the update runs, and the condition is tested again. The body may execute zero times. This form is useful when an index or count follows a regular pattern.

The boundaries and update jointly determine the visited values. for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) visits n values when n is nonnegative. An index declared in the initialization is local to the loop. Equivalent while code must keep the initialization before the loop and the update in the correct place.
i takes values 2, 4, 6, and 8 in the body. total becomes 2, 6, 12, and 20. After the last body, the update produces 10 and the condition fails. The loop-local i cannot be read afterward.

Using an inclusive bound when an exclusive one is required adds an extra iteration. Updating the counter in both the header and body can skip values. A semicolon after the header creates an empty body.
Write a for loop that sums 1 through 5. Answer: initialize sum to 0, loop i = 1 while i <= 5, add i, and increment i. The result is 15. State what happens if the bound is 0.
